title: Auditions set for next theater musical
text:
The Jamestown Community Theatre has scheduled auditions for its upcoming production of “Merrily We Roll Along” in November, which will mark the first performance of the troupe’s 36th season.
The play, with music and lyrics by Stephen Sondheim and book by George Furth, tells the story of fictional composer Franklin Shepard, who has achieved tremendous professional success at great personal cost.
The action unfolds in reverse, leading toward the story’s origin, when Frank and his friends are young and full of hope. The score includes some of Sondheim’s most memorable hits, such as “Old Friends,” “Our Time,” “Not a Day Goes By” and the show-stopping “Franklin Shepard, Inc.”
“Merrily” features a memorable supporting cast, with characters such as Charley Kringas, a role that has attracted numerous stars, including Jesse Tyler Ferguson, Raul Esparza, Lin-Manuel Miranda and Daniel Radcliffe.
Auditions will be held by appointment Thursday, Sept. 3, at the recreation center.
Auditions are open to anyone in grade 5 and up. There are six adult leads, one child lead, numerous featured singing and speaking roles and ensemble opportunities. The film version, available on Netflix, is rated PG-13; the stage production is recommended for audiences at least 10 years old.
One can register by e-mailing jamestowncommunitytheatreRI@gmail.com for preparation materials and a character list. Use the subject “Merrily Auditions: (Name).” If registering a participant in grades 5-12, include the child’s grade level. If registering multiple people, send one e-mail per registrant rather than one per family.
Auditions will occur by appointment in groups. For children in grades 5-8, initial auditions will include singing. Adults and highschoolers will be asked to both sing and read a short monologue. Audition materials will be provided upon sign-up. Finalists for lead and featured roles will be invited to callbacks (Sept. 8 and 10), which may involve additional singing, reading from the script and dancing.
Performances are scheduled for Nov. 19-22.
The show’s storyline spans several decades, and the protagonist is seen from college through middle age. Accordingly, actors “appearing as” age is not fixed. Additionally, some adult characters may be played by teenagers.
All who accept roles in the cast will be required to register and pay a $30 membership fee. Actors also may be required to provide their own base costumes, often drawing from their own wardrobes.
Additionally, parents of participating children ages 17 and under are asked to volunteer in one or more ways, such as taking turns providing supervision during rehearsals and performances, helping with sets and designing costumes.
The production will be directed by Ricky Martin with music direction by Joseph Carvalho and choreography by Amanda Del Vecchio, Sam Mathias and Elle Roy.
